refined_brief: Source-grounded 4:3 black/white abstracts with framed subfigures, appropriate quantitative plots, explained terminology, consistent spacing and right-aligned source credits.
central_argument: The 2017 demonstration makes seat-pressure history available during and after a ride; the 2019 modular design combines pressure and camera geometry for contextual posture feedback.
source_evidence: INTERACT 2017, pages 421-422: two under-seat force-sensitive resistors feed a Genuino microcontroller, Bluetooth Low Energy dashboard and mobile-internet remote storage. Integer readings 0-1023 are divided into four equal bins; dashboard views show the past three minutes and whole-ride pressure variation with duration. TEI 2019, pages 445-449: six seat force-sensitive resistors and two analog-to-digital converters, a camera tracking four reference markers (helmet/head top, chin, both shoulders), separate Raspberry Pi modules and a central Raspberry Pi connected through WebSockets. Relative upper-body geometry and seat-load distribution describe forward/back and left/right lean, shoulder tilt and head stoop. Contour feedback compares current posture to a reference, with duration/history relevant to interpretation.
limitations: The 2017 bins are pressure-reading intervals, not posture classes. Pattern fills are a new monochrome explanatory key, not a claim about the original interface appearance. Traces, contours and hardware drawings are schematic. The 2019 paper reports modules and a design; full integration, riding evaluation and learning remain proposed future work in that paper. The project overview does not pool evaluation results or claim health efficacy. Four markers are camera-tracked reference points, not four additional sensors.
